system_type: 24 V DC solar home system (DC appliances, MPPT charge controller, LFP battery, no AC inverter)

design_inputs.sun_source: NASA POWER hourly GHI, Maiduguri, 2014-2023 (10 years, data/): lowest long-term monthly mean = month 8 at 5.07 kWh/m2/day; annual mean 5.92; worst single month 8/2022 at 4.72. Horizontal irradiance, as in the PV model.
design_inputs.battery_selection_reason: Selected from src/sizing_map.py on NASA POWER 2014-2023 with both ageing models: 400 Wp + 1.92 kWh gives the SABIL controller 13 hours of lost critical power in 10 years (0 in 8 of the 10 years) against 110 for the standard controller; adding PV is cheaper than adding battery to ride through the cloudiest rainy seasons (2022). Energy balance alone gives 350 Wp + 1.28 kWh.

notes.pv_derate: Losses NOT modelled hourly: soiling incl. Harmattan dust 5% x DC wiring and mismatch 3% = 0.92. Temperature loss is modelled hourly from NOCT and pv_temp_coeff_per_c, so it is not in pv_derate.
notes.inverter_eff: DC system, so this is the distribution efficiency between battery/PV bus and appliances: MPPT 0.97 x wiring and DC-DC 0.98 = 0.95. Key name kept for the integration contract.
notes.design_psh_h: Lowest monthly mean of daily horizontal irradiation, computed by sizing.py from the NASA POWER hourly year (see design_inputs.sun_source). Replaced the earlier profilesolar.com estimate (5.8 h), which was optimistic.
notes.pv_temp_loss_design: Design-month estimate only: cell ~55 C in operation (NOCT 45 C, ambient ~30 C), (55-25) x 0.35%/C = 10.5%. The hourly simulation computes it exactly.
notes.pv_temp_coeff_per_c: Typical mono-PERC datasheet value -0.35 %/C. TO CONFIRM with the chosen module datasheet.
notes.battery_eol_capacity_frac: The battery is sized so that at end of life (80% capacity) it still covers the night load. This links sizing to the ageing model.
